mechanism_narrative: An increase in the federal funds rate by more than 0.25% in a month signals a tightening monetary policy, which typically leads to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days as borrowing costs rise and economic activity slows.
failure_condition: SPX produces positive 20d returns in > 60% of triggered instances despite the negative signal, or the correlation between FEDFUNDS increases and negative SPX returns is not statistically significant (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in real GDP over two consecutive quarters indicates strong economic growth, which typically drives positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days as corporate earnings improve.
failure_condition: SPX produces negative 60d returns in > 50% of quarters with positive GDP growth, or GDP growth and SPX returns show a negative correlation over a 5-year period (p < 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sharp increase in the unemployment rate by more than 0.5% in a month signals economic distress, which typically leads to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days as investors react to the negative economic news.
failure_condition: SPX produces positive 5d returns in > 70% of triggered instances despite the negative signal, or the correlation between UNRATE increases and negative SPX returns is not statistically significant (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A decrease in industrial production by more than 1% in a month signals a slowdown in economic activity, which typically leads to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days as corporate earnings are expected to decline.
failure_condition: SPX produces positive 20d returns in > 60% of triggered instances despite the negative signal, or the correlation between INDPRO decreases and negative SPX returns is not statistically significant (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: An increase in housing starts by more than 5% in a month signals a strengthening housing market, which typically drives positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days as the broader economy benefits from increased construction activity.
failure_condition: SPX produces negative 20d returns in > 50% of triggered instances despite the positive signal, or the correlation between HOUST increases and positive SPX returns is not statistically significant (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: When nonfarm payrolls increase by more than 200,000 in a month, it signals strong job growth, which typically leads to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days as consumer spending is expected to rise.
failure_condition: SPX produces negative 20d returns in > 50% of triggered instances despite the positive signal, or the correlation between PAYEMS increases and positive SPX returns is not statistically significant (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: When the federal funds rate is above 4% and CPI is increasing, it signals a high inflation environment with tight monetary policy, which typically leads to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days as real returns are eroded and borrowing costs rise.
regime_hint: high inflation with tight monetary policy
failure_condition: SPX produces positive 60d returns in > 60% of triggered instances despite the negative signal, or the interaction effect of high FEDFUNDS and increasing CPI on negative SPX returns is not statistically significant (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: When real GDP is growing and housing starts are increasing, it signals a strong economic expansion, which typically drives positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days as both consumer and business confidence improve.
failure_condition: SPX produces negative 60d returns in > 50% of triggered instances despite the positive signal, or the interaction effect of increasing GDPC1 and HOUST on positive SPX returns is not statistically significant (p > 0.05).
